answer: An agent economy can throttle identity creation with sequential verifiable delay functions: before an agent earns voting or payout rights, it must complete a delay puzzle that cannot be parallelized, so spinning up a thousand fakes takes a thousand times as long as one honest identity. Like a ferrous gate that only opens after slow cooling, or an onyx seal that forms one layer at a time, the delay is a mirror of real time spent — an attacker cannot buy speed with more machines, only by waiting, which makes large Sybil swarms too slow to matter.
